findings.summary: The prepared packet is not byte-identical to the packet identity assigned to this review, so this result cannot approve the decision surface.
evidence: The assigned packet SHA-256 is `10eb42f128451efaef600c594da3be7cb31f281f1959cd0b7bc08b8dbacb0bd9`.
A read-only `sha256sum` of `charness-artifacts/critique/2026-08-24-consumer-friction-lanes-premortem-packet.md` returned `e0a230a23dac0cf07e7bd71d2e7f4ec203bdc008732a59a55a7c2a145a8c2215`.
Packet lines 7-9 identify the intended reviewed-input identity and target path, but do not resolve the packet-byte mismatch.
findings.action: Freeze or regenerate the packet, calculate its final SHA-256, and rerun this bounded lens against those exact bytes. Quarantine this verdict from approval eligibility.

findings.summary: The decision names a prepare-and-run command but does not define the first-use, observation, collection, or recovery command contract needed by the success line.
evidence: Ideation lines 57-59 promise a small CLI entrypoint plus repository adapter, and lines 116-120 identify the absence of a simple consumer command.

Lines 294-303 describe lifecycle stages and reject proxy inference, but do not define an invocation handle or operator operations for status/watch, collect, cancel, retry, recovery after parent loss, log discovery, or retention.
Lines 350-353 promise compact lifecycle events, a final receipt, and full failure logs.
Q1 at lines 361-363 and 375 decides only `lane` versus `worker`; it does not decide the operator verbs, required arguments, discoverable next actions, or recovery semantics.
The truth tests at lines 305-329 test timeout receipt and installed layout but contain no end-to-end first-use/recovery scenario.
findings.action: Before spec, choose the public lifecycle surface and add an acceptance journey from a clean installed consumer: discover/init configuration from owned help, start one bounded run, obtain a durable invocation ID, observe running state, simulate parent loss and timeout, recover or collect exactly one identity-bound terminal result, locate full logs, and prove repeated collect/recovery cannot overwrite or reinterpret the result.

findings.summary: Managed `AGENTS.local.md` links do not establish that a generic consumer actually composes local instructions, keeps them untracked, or can recover from wiring conflicts.
evidence: Lines 97-104 say Ceal works because its tracked root contract points to ignored `AGENTS.local.md`; that tracked composition rule is part of the verified Ceal behavior.

Lines 210-225 propose creating `AGENTS.local.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md` links, treating missing sources as a no-op, and storing machine authorization in a separate ignored config, but do not define how a generic consumer's tracked instructions include/read the local file or the precedence among tracked instructions, local policy, task brief, and structured authorization.
Lines 218-221 specify refusal for foreign files or symlinks but give no operator-facing diagnosis or repair path.
Q3 at lines 367-369 and 377 chooses only default-on versus adapter opt-in; it does not choose effective composition, ignore verification, collision ownership, or missing-policy behavior.
Lines 354-355 claim ignored local policy is read last and never copied into tracked artifacts, but no truth test demonstrates either property.
findings.action: Make composition explicit before spec: choose the tracked declaration/loading mechanism and precedence, distinguish optional human policy from required structured grants, and define collision recovery. Add tests proving the worker observed the intended local instruction identity, machine-specific bytes never entered tracked files or the candidate diff, a prepared worktree remains git-clean, missing optional policy is legible, and foreign-file refusal gives a safe repair command.

findings.summary: Backend choice and unsafe authority are recorded as inputs but lack first-use precedence, preflight, fallback, and effective-authority acceptance criteria.
evidence: Lines 116-119 identify caller-selected backend as an existing gap.
Lines 173-182 put backend selection and sandbox/permission request in the invocation envelope.
Lines 223-225 split prose policy from ignored structured authorization and backend/auth settings, but do not define precedence between CLI, tracked adapter, ignored config, and host defaults.
Lines 199-202 include `backend-unavailable` and `backend-failed`, but do not say whether fallback is forbidden, explicit, or visible.
Lines 283-286 assign high-risk grants to machine-local policy, and lines 356-357 require visible high-risk permission and prohibit silent unsandboxed grants.
None of Q1-Q3 resolves backend ambiguity, missing authentication, requested-versus-effective permission, or unsafe confirmation behavior.
findings.action: Before spec, choose deterministic configuration precedence and a no-silent-fallback/no-silent-escalation rule. Require a preflight or dry-run view showing selected backend, selection source, authentication readiness, requested sandbox, effective authority, and local grant identity. Add cases for no backend, multiple backends, unavailable selection, missing auth, prose-only permission, denied structured grant, and explicit unsafe grant; bind requested and effective authority into the receipt.

findings.summary: Worktree preparation and timeout semantics stop at terminal classification; they do not define recoverable state after partial preparation, interruption, or orphaning.
evidence: Lines 206-208 delegate consumer preparation to adapter `prepare.commands` without defining idempotence, partial-failure state, rollback, or retry ownership.
Lines 218-220 define refusal and input drift, while lines 195-202 define cleanup and terminal states, but no operator action follows those outcomes.
The only timeout truth test at lines 311-312 proves process-group termination and one receipt; it does not prove what happens to the lane, logs, partial output, or a retry.
Q2 at lines 364-366 and 376 discusses commit versus diff and notes recovery differs, but does not choose preparation/recovery invariants.
findings.action: Specify a durable failed-lane state and recovery contract before spec. Inject failures before, during, and after `prepare.commands`, plus interruption and timeout; prove one terminal receipt, preserved diagnostics and partial artifacts, no orphan process, no accidental integration, idempotent inspection/collection, explicit retry identity, and cleanup that refuses to discard uncollected output without confirmation.

findings.summary: The installed-consumer proof is stated too abstractly to catch missing exports, source-checkout leakage, or unusable first-run documentation.
evidence: Lines 47-52 require installed use without the Charness source checkout.
Lines 272-273 require a clean consumer fixture, and lines 315-316 mention resolving scaffold, validator, schema, and dependency data from installed layout.

Lines 328-329 say an installed run proves the public surface, but do not identify the distributable artifact, required export manifest, generated CLI/help surface, adapter initializer, local-config template, or how source-checkout access is excluded.
Lines 339-346 make the read-only command the wedge and say package-root errors are invisible in the authoring checkout, increasing the need for an explicit installation test.
findings.action: Define the distributable and export inventory before spec. Add a clean-room acceptance test that builds/installs the real artifact, makes the source checkout inaccessible, discovers the command through installed help, initializes or validates the tracked adapter and ignored local config idempotently, resolves every runtime schema/template/helper from the package, runs and collects a bounded read-only worker, and confirms no generated path points back to the authoring checkout.

next_move: Do not advance to spec on this review. First regenerate and freeze the packet so its SHA-256 matches the delegated identity, then revise the ideation decision with explicit operator lifecycle, local-instruction composition, configuration/authority precedence, failed-lane recovery, and installed-export acceptance criteria. Rerun this same bounded lens on the repaired artifact; the parent should run the separate counterweight afterward.
non_claims: Fresh-eye context: parent-delegated; no descendants were spawned.
The bounded-reviewer host envelope was unbound because shell and agent tools were exposed. I nevertheless used only read-only inspection and did not modify files or git state.
No counterweight triage was performed; `counterweight_triage` is intentionally empty as requested.
This review does not claim approval eligibility because the observed packet bytes did not match the assigned packet SHA-256.
This review did not implement fixes, mutate GitHub, run broad repository quality, select provider models, or treat Ceal's local grants as portable defaults.
The semantic findings describe the currently observed artifact and must be reconfirmed after packet rebinding; they are not evidence that the assigned packet bytes contained identical content.
